examDifficulty.heading: Is the Loyalty Management Accredited Professional Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: It is a moderate exam. Most questions are about how points are earned and spent, how members move between tiers, and how program processes apply the rules.
bullets: About 65% to pass, roughly 39 correct answers. Check the official guide for the current figure.
Programme design. Currencies, tiers, benefits, promotions and vouchers.
Rules engine. How transaction journals and program processes award and redeem points.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Build a small programme in a trial org with two tiers and a promotion, then post a few transactions. Before you book. Aim for 75% or more on practice tests.

examFormat.heading: Loyalty Management Accredited Professional Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: Accredited Professional exams are taken online. Here is what to expect:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Most questions describe a loyalty need, such as double points for a weekend or keeping gold status for another year, and ask how to set it up.
bestWayToPass: Learn the currencies: Qualifying points decide tier status. Non-qualifying points are spent on rewards.
Understand transaction journals: Every purchase or activity is posted as a journal, then processed by rules.
Know program processes: They hold the rules for accrual, redemption and tier changes.
Practise promotions: Bonus points, limits and eligibility for a set of members.

certificationCard.description: This exam tests how you set up Salesforce Loyalty Management: programmes, points and tiers, accrual and redemption rules, promotions, vouchers, partners and reporting.

keyConcepts.h2: Loyalty Management AP: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Program Design: Tiers & Points
blocks.body: A **loyalty program** holds everything about one scheme. **Program currencies** are the points members collect. **Qualifying** points count toward tier status. **Non-qualifying** points can be spent on rewards but don't affect tier. **Tier groups** contain **tiers**, such as Silver, Gold and Platinum, each with thresholds and **benefits** like free delivery or lounge access. Tiers can be reviewed on a set schedule, and rules decide whether members move up, stay, or drop down.

blocks.heading: Points Accrual & Redemption Rules
blocks.body: Every purchase, flight or other activity is recorded as a **transaction journal**. **Program processes** contain the rules that act on journals, for example: give 1 point per dollar spent, or 2 points per dollar for Gold members. Redemption works the same way: a journal for a reward triggers rules that take points away. Points can be set to **expire** after a period, and the **member's ledger** shows every change to their balance, so balances can always be explained.

blocks.heading: Promotions & Member Engagement
blocks.body: **Promotions** encourage certain behaviour, like double points on a weekend or bonus points for a first purchase in a new category. They can be limited to certain members, products or dates, and capped so they don't cost too much. **Vouchers** give members a discount or reward they can use later. **Badges** and **games** can add fun elements. Members can see their points, tier and vouchers through a member portal built on Experience Cloud.

blocks.heading: Partner Integration & Ecosystem
blocks.body: Many programmes let members earn and spend points with **partners**, such as an airline programme that gives points for hotel stays. **Loyalty program partners** are set up with their own terms, and the brand can track how many points each partner has issued or redeemed, which is used for billing between companies. Partners usually send transactions through APIs, and the same journals and rules then apply.

blocks.heading: Analytics & Program Reporting
blocks.body: Brands need to know whether the programme pays off. Reports and the **Loyalty Analytics** app show active members, points issued and redeemed, tier movement and promotion results. **Points liability**, the value of unspent points, is an important finance number. Combining loyalty data with purchase and marketing data, for example in **Data Cloud**, helps target the right offers to the right members.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Loyalty Management Accredited Professional Exam
scenarioTips.intro: Most questions start with a programme rule written in plain words. Work out which currency, tier, process or promotion makes that rule happen.

blocks.heading: Loyalty Program Setup
blocks.body: Programme, currencies, tier groups and tiers come first. Benefits attach to tiers.

blocks.heading: Accrual & Redemption Rules
blocks.body: Activity is posted as transaction journals. Program processes apply the rules to award or remove points.

blocks.heading: Member Enrollment & Lifecycle
blocks.body: Members join, earn, move between tiers and may become inactive. Expiry and tier review rules handle this over time.

blocks.heading: Partner Management
blocks.body: Partners send transactions too. Track points issued and redeemed per partner for billing.

blocks.heading: Loyalty Analytics
blocks.body: Watch points liability, redemption rate and tier movement, as well as promotion results.

sampleQuestions.question: Members should reach Gold status based on points earned from flights, but points from a credit card partner should only be spendable. How should currencies be set up?
options: Use one currency and ignore tiers
sampleQuestions.explanation: Qualifying points count toward tiers. Non-qualifying points can be spent but don't change status.
whyWrong: Making all points qualifying lets credit card spend drive status.
Making all points non-qualifying means nothing drives tier status.
Ignoring tiers removes a core part of the programme.

sampleQuestions.question: A member buys a $120 jacket in store. How is this recorded before points are given?
options: As a transaction journal for the processes to act on
As a partner organisation record on the programme
sampleQuestions.explanation: Purchases are posted as transaction journals, and the rules in program processes award the points.
whyWrong: Partners are other companies in the programme.
Vouchers are rewards to use later.

sampleQuestions.question: Gold members should earn 2 points per dollar, while others earn 1. Where is this rule set?
options: In the voucher definition held against the promotion
In a program process rule checking the tier
sampleQuestions.explanation: Program processes hold accrual rules and can use conditions like tier.
whyWrong: Partner settings cover partner terms, not tier rates.

sampleQuestions.question: The brand wants double points on all purchases over one holiday weekend, capped at 500 bonus points per member. What should be used?
options: A manual points adjustment for each member
sampleQuestions.explanation: Promotions can run for set dates, change how points are earned, and include caps.
whyWrong: Tiers are status levels, not time-limited offers.
A new currency isn't needed for bonus points.

sampleQuestions.question: Points should disappear if they aren't used within 24 months. What should be configured?
options: Points expiry rules for the currency
Deleting the members who are inactive
sampleQuestions.explanation: Expiry rules remove points after a set time; which also helps control points liability.

sampleQuestions.question: A member asks why their balance dropped last month. Where can an agent see every change to the balance?
sampleQuestions.explanation: The ledger records each earning, redemption and expiry, so balances can be explained.
whyWrong: The partner list doesn't show a member's balance.
Tier definitions describe tiers, not one member's history.

sampleQuestions.question: Members of a hotel programme should also earn points when they rent cars from a partner company. What should be set up?
options: A second programme for car rental
sampleQuestions.explanation: Partners can be part of a programme, sending transactions that earn points under agreed terms.
whyWrong: A second programme splits the member's points.

sampleQuestions.question: Finance wants to know the value of all unspent points. What is this called?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Points liability is the value of points members could still redeem, which finance must account for.
whyWrong: Redemption rate shows how much is spent.

sampleQuestions.question: Gold members get free delivery. Where is this recorded?
options: As a benefit on the Gold tier
sampleQuestions.explanation: Benefits attach to tiers so members get them while in that tier.

sampleQuestions.question: A member reaches Gold in March. When should the programme check whether they keep Gold?
options: Only at the point when they telephone the support team
At the tier review date set in the tier rules
sampleQuestions.explanation: Tier rules define when status is reviewed and what is needed to keep it.
whyWrong: Tiers usually need to be re-earned.
Login checks aren't how tiers work.

sampleQuestions.question: Members should see their points, tier and vouchers online. What is the usual way?
options: A weekly PDF statement sent by email
A portal built on Experience Cloud
sampleQuestions.explanation: An Experience Cloud site can show members their loyalty details at any time.
whyWrong: A PDF is out of date between statements.
Calling support costs more and is slower.
Chatter groups aren't for member accounts.

sampleQuestions.question: After a promotion, the marketing team wants to know if it increased spend. What should they look at?
options: The colour scheme used across the member portal
sampleQuestions.explanation: Reporting on promotion performance shows whether it changed member behaviour.
whyWrong: Tier count doesn't measure the promotion.

sampleQuestions.question: A member returns a product they earned 120 points on. What should happen?
options: A transaction journal that removes the points
Move the member down into a lower tier straight away
sampleQuestions.explanation: Returns should be posted as journals so rules can reverse the points earned.
whyWrong: Tier changes follow tier rules, not every return.
Leaving the points rewards a purchase that didn't stick.

sampleQuestions.question: The brand wants to send members personalised offers based on loyalty, purchase and web data together. What helps most?
options: Bringing the data together in Data Cloud
Asking all of the members to fill in a feedback survey
sampleQuestions.explanation: Data Cloud combines data from many sources into one profile, which supports better targeting.

sampleQuestions.question: A member earns a $10 reward to use on their next order. What should be issued?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Vouchers hold rewards like discounts that members can use later.
